McDOWELL LEE Secretary 3156 JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE, 1999 28th Day SENATE MESSAGE On motion of Representative Graham, the House concurred in and adopted the Senate amendment to the bill, HB42, said Senate amendment being as follows: A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT Reopening, for a certain time, the Teachers' Retirement System (TRS) and the Employees' Retirement System (ERS) for purchase of certain service credit by certain active members for certain prior service rendered to an employer who may join the TRS pursuant to Section 16-25-10.7, Code of Alabama 1975, but has not elected to participate. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. Active and contributing members of the Teachers' Retirement System (TRS) or the Employees' Retirement System (ERS) may claim and purchase service credit in the system not to exceed eight years for any period of prior service while they were full-time employees of an employer who is authorized to join the TRS pursuant to Section 16-25-10.7, Code of Alabama 1975, but has not elected to participate. The certification of any prior service claimed by the members under this act shall conform to applicable administrative rules and procedures of the TRS or ERS. Members shall receive credit for the prior service when they remit to the system the contributions required by Section 2 of this act. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no member of the system shall receive credit for any service that the member is already credited with in the system or any other public retirement plan, with the exception of the federal Social Security program. Section 2. Any member who is eligible to purchase service credit in the TRS or ERS under Section 1 of this act shall pay to the Secretary-Treasurer of the system, within one year from the effective date of this act, for the claimed service, a sum equal to the full actuarially required cost for each year of service credit purchased as determined by the actuary for the system. Section 3. This act shall become effective on the first day of the third month following its passage and approval by the Governor, or its otherwise becoming law.

BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That there is hereby created the Joint Interim Legislative Committee to evaluate and make recommendations on the potential year 2000 (Y2K) computer system problems in state government. The committee shall be composed of five members of each house of the Legislature, to be appointed by the presiding officer of each house. An advisory panel composed of the Secretary-Treasurer of the Retirement Systems of Alabama, the Directors of the Information Services and Risk Management Divisions of the Finance Department, the State Finance Director, the Industrial Relations Director, the Commissioners of Revenue, Medicaid, Human Resources, and Corrections, the State Health Officer, and the State Personnel Director shall attend meetings of the committee and inform the committee of any progress and deterrents to progress on the Y2K problems. The Chair and Vice Chair of the committee shall be elected at the first meeting of the committee which shall be called by the Speaker of the House no later than five days after the effective date of this resolution. The committee shall study the potential Y2K problems in state government and develop a plan for correcting the problems. Upon the request of the chair, the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House of Representatives shall provide the clerical assistance necessary for the work of the committee. The committee shall meet on call of the chair throughout 1999 and shall give an initial report of its perception of potential Y2K problems to the Legislature not later than the fifth legislative day of the 1999 Regular Session. The committee shall stand dissolved and discharged of its duties on January 1, 2000. Each member of the committee shall be entitled to his or her regular legislative compensation, his or her per diem, and travel expenses for each day of attendance at a committee meeting which shall be paid out of any funds appropriated to the use of the Legislature, upon warrants drawn on the State Comptroller upon requisitions signed by the chair of the committee. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no legislative member of the committee shall receive additional legislative compensation or per diem when the Legislature is in session or if a member is being paid any other payments on the same dates for attendance of other business. MOTION TO SUSPEND RULES ADOPTED On motion of Representative Hooper, the rules were suspended in order to take up for immediate consideration the resolution, HJR10.

WHEREAS, the Legislature of Alabama, while debating legislation imposing criminal penalties upon persons possessing open containers of alcoholic beverages in a motor vehicle, have observed that the rationale and justification of such legislation is questionable and may not best serve the interest of our citizens; and WHEREAS, our state and other states have been placed in a difficult posture due to Congressional mandates requiring the passage of such legislation in order to avoid the redirection of certain federal highway funds; and WHEREAS, we think the imposition of such a requirement may result in poor public policy and, most importantly, rather than assisting in the reduction of REGULAR SESSION 493 6th Day alcohol related motor vehicle accidents, actually discourage designated drivers and similar responsible behavior; and WHEREAS, this legislative body has consistently and unequivocally supported all efforts to enforce and strengthen laws related to driving under the influence, and we, like the U.S. Congress, strongly desire to adopt and enforce public policy which will eliminate drunk drivers; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the United States Congress is encouraged to review and reconsider current federal law which imposes a requirement upon the states to enact alcoholic beverage open container legislation. The Clerk of the House of Representatives is directed to provide a copy of this resolution to the President of the United States Senate, the Speaker of the United States House of Representatives, and to each member of the Alabama Congressional Delegation, so that each may be informed of our concern regarding this matter and our mutual desire to adopt appropriate and effective public policy which will effectively result in a reduction in deaths and injury from drunk driving. On motion of Representative Venable, the rules were suspended in order to take up immediate consideration of the foregoing resolution, HJR118.

"(7) For any licensee or the servants, agents, or employees of the same to be directly or indirectly employed by any other licensee engaged in the manufacture, storage, transportation, or sale of alcoholic beverages. "(8) For any person to knowingly sell any alcoholic beverages to any person engaged in the business of illegally selling alcoholic beverages. "(9) For any person to manufacture, transport, or import alcoholic beverages into this state, except in accordance with the reasonable rules and regulations of the board. This subdivision shall not prohibit the transportation of alcoholic beverages through the state or any dry county so long as the beverages are not for delivery therein, if the transportation is done in accordance with the reasonable rules and regulations of the board. "(10) For any person to fortify, adulterate, contaminate, or in any manner change the character or purity of alcoholic beverages from that as originally marketed by the manufacturer, except that a retail licensee on order from a customer may mix a chaser or other ingredients necessary to prepare a cocktail or mixed drink for on-premises consumption. "(11) For any person licensed to sell alcoholic beverages to offer to give any thing of value as a premium for the return of caps, stoppers, corks, stamps, or labels taken from any bottle, case, barrel, or package containing the alcoholic beverages, or to offer to give any thing of value as a premium or present to induce the purchase of the alcoholic beverages, or for any other purpose whatsoever in connection with the sale of the alcoholic beverages. This subdivision shall not apply to the return of any moneys specifically deposited for the return of the original containers to the owners of the containers. "(12) For any licensee or transporter for hire, servant, agent, or employee of the same, to transport any alcoholic beverages except in the original container, and for any transporter for hire to transport any alcoholic beverages within the state, unless the transporter holds a permit issued by the board. "(13) For any manufacturer, importer, or wholesaler, servant, agent, or employee of the same, to deliver any alcoholic beverages, except in vehicles bearing the name, address, and permit number of the manufacturer, importer, or wholesaler painted or affixed on each side of the vehicle in letters no smaller than four inches in height such information on each side of the vehicle as may be required by the board. "(14) For any person to sell alcoholic beverages within any dry county or county where the electors have voted against the sales, except in wet municipalities or as authorized by Section 28-3A-18. "(16) For any manufacturer, distiller, producer, importer, or distributor of alcoholic beverages to employ and maintain any person, who is not a full-time bona fide employee, as a resident sales agent, broker, or other like representative, for the purpose of promoting a sale, purchase, or acquisition of alcoholic beverages to or by the state or the board, or for any person who is not a full-time bona fide employee to act as an agent, broker, or representative of any manufacturer, distributor, producer, importer, or distiller for that purpose. "(17) For any person to sell, give away, or otherwise dispose of taxable alcoholic beverages within this state on which the required taxes have not been paid as required by law. "(18) For any wholesaler or retailer, or the servant, agent, or employee of the same, to sell, distribute, deliver, or to receive or store for sale or distribution within this state any alcoholic beverages unless there first has been issued by the board a manufacturer's license to the manufacturer of the alcoholic beverages or its designated representative or an importer license to the importer of the alcoholic beverages. "(19) For any person under the legal drinking age, as defined in Section 28-1-5, to attempt to purchase, to purchase, consume, possess, or to transport any alcoholic beverages within the state; provided, however, it shall not be unlawful for a person under the legal drinking age, as defined in Section 28-1-5, to be an employee of a wholesale licensee or an off-premises retail licensee of the board to handle, transport, or sell any beer or table wine if the person under the legal drinking age is acting within the line and scope of his or her employment while so acting. There must be an adult licensee, servant, agent, or employee of the same present at all times a licensed establishment is open for business. "(20) For any person, except where authorized by a local act or general act of local application, to buy, give away, sell, or serve for consumption on or off the premises, or to drink or consume any alcoholic beverages in any cafe, lunchroom, restaurant, hotel dining room, or other public place on Sunday after the hour of two o'clock A.M. "(21) Except where authorized by a local act or general act of local application, for the proprietor, keeper or operator of any cafe, lunchroom, restaurant, hotel dining room, or other public place to knowingly permit any person to give away, sell, or serve for consumption on or off the premises, or to drink or consume any alcoholic beverages on the premises of the cafe, lunchroom, restaurant, hotel dining room, or other public place on Sunday after the hour of two o'clock A.M. 2700 JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE, 2002 30th Day "(22) For a person under the age of 21 years to knowingly use or attempt to use a false, forged, deceptive, or otherwise nongenuine driver's license to obtain or attempt to obtain alcoholic beverages within this state. "(b)(1) Any violation of subdivisions (1) through (18) of subsection (a) of this section shall be a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100) nor more than one thousand dollars ($1,000), to which, at the discretion of the court or judge trying the case, may be added imprisonment in the county jail or at hard labor for the county for not more than six months for the first conviction; and, on the second conviction of a violation of the subdivisions, the offense shall, in addition to the aforementioned fine, be punishable by imprisonment or at hard labor for the county for not less than three months nor more than six months to be imposed by the court or judge trying the case; and, on the third conviction and every subsequent conviction of a violation of the subdivisions, the offense shall, in addition to a fine within the limits abovenamed, be punishable by imprisonment or at hard labor for the county for not less than six months nor more than 12 months. "(2) Any violation of any provision of subdivisions (19), (20), (21), and (22) of subsection (a) of this section shall be a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than fifty dollars ($50) nor more than five hundred dollars ($500), to which, at the discretion of the court or judge trying the case, may be added imprisonment in the county jail or at hard labor for the county for not more than three months. "In addition to the penalties otherwise provided for a violation of subdivisions (19) and (22) of subsection (a) of this section, upon conviction, including convictions in juvenile court or under the Youthful Offender Act, the offender's license to operate a motor vehicle in this state shall be surrendered by the offender to the judge adjudicating the case for a period of not less than three months nor more than six months. The judge shall forward a copy of the order suspending the license to the Department of Public Safety for enforcement purposes." Section 2. Although this bill would have as its purpose or effect the requirement of a new or increased expenditure of local funds, the bill is excluded from further requirements and application under Amendment 621 because the bill defines a new crime or amends the definition of an existing crime. Section 3. This act shall become effective on the first day of the third month following its passage and approval by the Governor, or its otherwise becoming law. SUBSTITUTE ADOPTED And the substitute was adopted. REGULAR SESSION 2701 30th Day

Senator Mitchell offered the following substitute for the Bill, HB 45, to-wit: 233 NINTH DAY SUBSTITUTE FOR HB 45 A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT Providing for in-state travel expenses of certain state officials and amending Section 36-7- 20 of the Code of Alabama 1975; and providing for the use of certain incidental travel bonuses by state officials and employees. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. Section 36-7-20 of the Code of Alabama 1975, is amended to read as follows: “§36-7-20. “(a) The amount allowable to a person traveling inside the State of Alabama in the service of the state or any of its depart­ ments, institutions, boards, bureaus, commissions, councils, committees, or other like agencies for expenses other than transportation may be fixed by the Governor at not less than fifty dollars ($50) nor more than seventy-five dollars ($75) per day, and such this maximum or limit when fixed from time to time shall be uniform in operation as to all persons traveling within the state on official business. However, members of the Legislature shall be excluded from this section. “(b) No travel allowance shall be paid for a trip of less than six hours’ duration. For travel which does not require an over­ night stay, the traveler shall be paid a meal allowance of 15 percent of the regular per diem rate for a trip of from six to 12 hours’ duration, and for travel in excess of 12 hours’ duration, the traveler shall be paid one meal allowance and one-fourth of the per diem allowance. “(c) The per diem allowance shall not be paid to an employee stationed at the same place in the state for a period in excess of two consecutive months. After two consecutive months the amount of the allowance shall be reduced to 75 percent of the reg­ ular per diem rate per day. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this section shall not apply to officers and employees of the State of Alabama when they incur expenses representing the State of Alabama in the encouragement and promotion of trade or industrial development. On those occasions, when the representation is properly approved, those persons shall be reimbursed for the actual expenses incurred and paid by them if the representation is approved in advance in writing by the Governor or by the Director of Finance when so designated by the Governor. “(d) This section shall not apply to examiners or other persons designated by the Commissioner of Insurance to examine or cause to be examined the domestic insurance corporations qualified in this state when the expense incurred by those persons shall be paid by, collected, or received from the corporations examined under Section 27-2-25. “(e) This section shall be optional with the employing agency in those instances where the employee is required to attend training sessions, schools, seminars or other like group functions at a facility when it would serve the best interests of both the state and the employee, or in those instances when the employee is assigned to assist in suppressing on-going natural disaster situations, or other emergencies. In those cases, the cost of meals and per diem may be paid as set forth herein or by the employing agency of the state directly to the contract facility furnishing the service, but the costs of these services shall not exceed the amount allowable to the individual employee for in-state travel. “(f) For purposes of applying this section to members of the Legislature, each of the following shall apply: “(1) The presiding officer of the house to which the member belongs shall determine if the travel is in the service of the state. “(2) In connection with the same travel, members of the Legislature shall receive per diem under this section except in either of the following instances: “a. For attendance on special or regular session days or committee meeting days of the Legislature when otherwise compen­ sated pursuant to law. “b. For attendance on interim committee meeting days of the Legislature when otherwise compensated pursuant to law. “(3) Travel means a departure from the place of residence of the member of the Legislature.” Section 2. Any other law to the contrary notwithstanding, a public official or a public employee may receive, obtain, or oth­ erwise convert to personal use a bonus that is incidental to travel in the performance of official duties of the public official or public employee if the bonus is individual in nature and not able to be transferred to another unrelated individual or to the state, or a county, municipality, or governmental entity. This section is declaratory of and does not constitute a change in existing law. Section 3. This act shall become effective on the first day of the third month following its passage and approval by the Gov­ ernor, or its otherwise becoming law. Which was adopted.

The Standing Committee on Local Legislation No. 1 reported the following substitute for the Bill, SB 53, to-wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR SB 53 A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT Relating to Montgomery County; authorizing referendum elections to determine whether alcoholic beverages may be sold or dispensed on Sunday within Montgomery County. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. This act shall apply only in Montgomery County. Section 2. (a) The voters of Montgomery County may authorize the sale of alcoholic beverages within the county on Sunday by an election pursuant to this act, in the following manner: (1) The judge of probate of the county shall call an election for the county to determine the sentiment of the voters of the county as to whether or not alcoholic beverages can be legally sold or distributed on Sunday in the county. (2) Any election for Sunday sales of alcoholic beverages shall contain the following question on the ballot to be used for such election, and the question shall be in the following form: “Do you favor the legal sale and distribution of alcoholic beverages 159 SIXTH DAY within this county on Sunday after 12 o’clock noon? Yes ___. No ___.” (b) The election shall be held and the officers appointed to hold the election in the manner provided by law, and the returns thereof tabulated and results certified as provided by law for county elections. Any Sunday sales election shall be held as provided in this act or at the same time of the primary, general, or countywide election next succeeding the date of passage of this act, except as provided herein. (c) Notice of the election shall be given by the judge of probate by publication or by posting the notice at the courthouse apprising the voters of the county, at least three weeks before the date of the election, that an election shall be held to determine whether alcoholic beverages may be sold in the county on Sunday. The cost of the election shall be paid out of the general fund of the county. (d) Only qualified voters may vote in the election. If a majority of the voters of the county voting in the election vote “Yes,” alcoholic beverages can be legally sold, distributed, and consumed within the county on Sunday after the hour of 12 o’clock noon until the county changes its status from wet to dry. (e) If a majority of the voters voting in the election vote “No,” alcoholic beverages may not be sold or dispensed in the county (except in municipalities which presently permit the sale of alcoholic beverages on Sunday) on Sunday after the hour of 2 o’clock a.m., except as otherwise authorized by law or by a subsequent election which legalizes the sale and dispensing of alcoholic bever­ ages on Sunday. (f) Any election shall be held not less than 30 nor more than 45 days from the date of passage of the act, and where possible the date may be extended by the judge of probate for not more than 45 additional days to permit the election to be held at the time of a primary, general, or countywide election. Section 3. All laws or parts of laws which conflict with this act are repealed. Section 4. This act shall become effective immediately upon its passage and approval by the Governor, or upon its otherwise becoming a law. Which was adopted.

context_synopsis: A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT Requiring the agency which is the employer of a state employee to timely inform the employee in writing of any potentially detrimental information placed in the personnel file of the employee. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. Notwithstanding any other laws, rules, or regulations to the contrary, when a document pertaining to disciplinary action, including, but not limited to, written reprimands, suspensions, notes pertaining to oral reprimands or counselings regarding a state employee, or notes pertaining to matters that may be used regarding the employee in a disciplinary action are placed in the employee's personnel file, the agency which is the employer shall supply a copy of the documentation to the employee no later than 10 days after its inclusion in his or her personnel file. In the event that the information is not provided to the employee within 10 days as herein required, the reprimands or notes shall be removed from the employee's file and shall not be used against the employee in any future proceeding or disciplinary action. Section 2. This act shall become effective immediately upon its passage and approval by the Governor, or its otherwise becoming a law. Which was adopted.

context_synopsis: CREATING THE CALHOUN COUNTY EL­ ECTED AND APPOINTED OFFICIALS SALARY COMMIS­ SION. BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That there is established in Calhoun County, the Calhoun County Elected and Appointed Officials Salary Commission, hereinafter referred to as “the commission.” The commission shall be composed of nine (9) members who shall be residents of the county: two members from government; five members from the business community including: one lawyer, one proprietor, one salary administrator, one personnel manager, one editor of a newspaper published in Calhoun County; one educator; and one retired person. The commission members shall be appointed by, and serve at the pleasure of the Calhoun County Legislative Delegation. The chair shall be selected by the membership and shall preside over all meetings. The commission shall make its own rules for the conduct of its business. The initial meeting shall be held within 30 days after the last appointment is made and thereafter at the call of the chair and within the rules of the commission. Members of the commission shall serve without compensation and their terms shall expire on January 1, 2002, at which time the commission members shall stand discharged from any further duties. The general purpose of the commission is to provide information and recommendations regarding salaries and compensation of all elected and appointed city and county officials within Calhoun County. The specific objectives of the commission shall be prescribed by the Calhoun County Legislative Delegation. On motion of Senator Marsh, the Resolution, HJR47, was concurred in and adopted by the Senate.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. The following amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, is proposed and shall become valid as a part of the Constitution when all requirements of this act are fulfilled: PROPOSED AMENDMENT (a) This amendment shall apply only to Mobile County. (b) For the purpose of this constitutional amendment, the term “prostitution” shall mean the commission by a person of any natural or unnatural sexual act, deviate sexual intercourse, or sexual contact for monetary consideration or other thing of value. (c) No person in the county shall commit an act of prostitu­ tion. (d) No person shall solicit, compel, or coerce any person to commit an act of prostitution. (e) No person shall agree to engage in an act of prostitution and give or accept monetary consideration or other marketable thing of value in furtherance of the agreement. (f) No person shall knowingly do any of the following: 2238 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, REGULAR SESSION 2001 27th Day - May 10, 2001 (1) Cause or aid a person to commit or engage in prostitu­ tion. (2) Procure or solicit patrons for prostitution. (3) Provide persons or premises for prostitution purposes. (4) Receive or accept money or other marketable thing of value pursuant to a prior agreement with any person whereby he or she participates or is to participate in the proceeds of any prostitution activity. (5) Operate or assist in the operation of a house of prostitu­ tion or a prostitution enterprise. (g) It shall be unlawful for the owner or manager of any ho- tel, motel, inn, boardinghouse, apartment house, or any lodging place or like kind to employ a person who has been convicted of aiding or abetting prostitution. (h) Each violation is a Class A misdemeanor. Section 2. An election upon the proposed amendment shall be held in accordance with Amendment 555 to the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, and the election laws of this state. Section 3. The appropriate election official shall assign a bal­ lot number for the proposed constitutional amendment on the elec­ tion ballot and shall set forth the following description of the sub- stance or subject matter of the proposed constitutional amendment: “Relating to Mobile County, proposing an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, to prohibit prostitution and to pro­ vide for a penalty. “Proposed by Act _________” This description shall be followed by the following lan­ guage: “Yes ( ) No ( ).”

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. The city council or other governing body of the City of Prattville, by resolution passed by simple majority, may regulate and permit the sale for on premises consumption only of alcoholic beverages on Sunday after 12:00 p.m. upon the licensed premises of retail licensees of the Alcoholic Beverage Control Board of the State of Alabama and of the City of Prattville serving the general public including, but not limited to, hotels with conference centers and golf courses located within the corporate limits of the city. Any licensee granted authority to sell alcoholic beverages on Sunday pursuant to this act shall be required to have all servers of alcoholic beverages complete responsible vendor training in the manner provided by the Alcoholic Beverage Control Board. Section 2. The provisions of this act are cumulative and supplemental to the present power and authority of the City of Prattville, and is not intended to, nor shall it be interpreted so as to repeal any existing power or authority of the City of Prattville now permitted under the general laws of the state, or under any local or special act of the Legislature. Section 3. Sections 1 and 2 of this act shall become operative only if approved by a majority of the qualified electors of the City of Prattville who vote in an election to be held on the day designated by the Mayor of the City of Prattville. The notice of the election shall be given by the mayor, and the election shall be held, conducted, and the results canvassed in the manner as other city elections. The question shall be, “Do you favor the adoption of Act ____, of the ______ Session of the Alabama Legislature? Yes ( ) No ( ).” The city shall pay any costs and expenses not otherwise reimbursed by a governmental agency which are incidental to the election. If a THIRD EXTRAORDINARY SESSION 425 8th Day - September 11, 2001 majority of the votes cast in the election are “Yes,” Sections 1 and 2 of this act shall become operative immediately. If the majority of the votes are “No,” this act shall be repealed and shall have no further effect. The Mayor of the City of Prattville shall certify the results of the election to the Secretary of State. Section 4. This act shall become effective immediately upon its passage and approval by the Governor, or its otherwise becoming a law. Which was adopted.

recovered_synopsis: MOURNING THE DEATH OF DR. ROBERT WALLACE MONTGOMERY. WHEREAS, herein recorded with deepest sorrow and regret is the death of Dr. Robert Wallace Montgomery of Auburn, Alabama, on July 20, 2001, at the age of 91 years; and WHEREAS, Dr. Montgomery was born in Wren, Alabama, on April 22, 1910; he and his beloved wife, the late Stella Etheredge Montgomery of Town Creek, were married from June 30, 1939, until parted by her death on July 4, 1981; and WHEREAS, he received his bachelor’s degree from Auburn University in 1932 and his doctorate from Ohio State University in 1952; and WHEREAS, Dr. Montgomery enjoyed a 42-year career at Auburn University and ably served as department head of Vocational and Adult Education from 1961 until his retirement as Professor Emeritus in 1981; and WHEREAS, throughout the years, Dr. Montgomery devoted considerable time to worthwhile organizations, including serving as president of the Alabama Rehabilitation Association and treasurer of the National Rehabilitation Association; and WHEREAS, he was recognized for his outstanding con­ tributions with many honors and awards and was named to the Voca­ tional Association Hall of Fame, received Ohio State’s Centennial Award and Auburn’s Outstanding Education Alumnus Award, and was an early and outspoken advocate of civil rights; and 212 THIRD EXTRAORDINARY SESSION 5th Day - September 5, 2001 WHEREAS, indeed, Dr. Montgomery was a truly commend­ able Alabamian who greatly contributed to the betterment of his com­ munity and our great state and his legacy will live on through the lives he touched; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Dr. Montgomery are his three children, Bob Montgomery, Linda C. Montgomery, and Ron Montgomery; four grandchildren, Jason Montgomery, Paige Burton, Adam Montgomery, and Becky Montgomery; one great- grandchild, Straton Porter; brother, Marion Montgomery; and sister, Irene Shoemaker; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA­ BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That even as his death is mourned with a deep sense of sadness and loss, the life and accomplishments of Dr. Robert Wallace Montgomery are herein celebrated, and it is directed that a copy of this resolution shall be pro­ vided to his family that they may know we sincerely share their great and grievous loss. Senator Little (T) then requested and received unanimous consent, pursuant to the provisions of Senate Rule 35(d), in order to consider the Resolution. And on motion of Senator Little (T), the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

WHEREAS, recorded with a sense of deep sorrow and loss is the death of former Alexander City businessman and civic leader Joseph Hunt Robinson at the age of 94 years; and WHEREAS, Mr. Robinson was a graduate of Alexander City High School and earned a Bachelor of Science Degree from the Uni­ versity of Alabama; he also exemplified the highest standards of pro­ fessionalism with his successful business, the Robinson Corporation Group, which owns the Robinson Iron Corporation, Robinson Foundry, Inc., Robinson-Latza Corporation, and Satterfield Machine Company; and WHEREAS, he was a founding member and peerless leader of the Alexander City Lions Club, which was organized in 1938; took the oath of office as an Alexander City councilman in 1947; named president of the Alexander City Council in 1948; and served with distinction as mayor of Alexander City from 1950 to 1956; and WHEREAS, in recognition of his contributions to the community, Mr. Robinson was named the Alexander City Man of the 216 THIRD EXTRAORDINARY SESSION 5th Day - September 5, 2001 Year by the Alexander City Chamber of Commerce, the third recipient of that award; and, for his outstanding contributions to the Boy Scouts of America, earned the Silver Beaver Award, the highest award given to an adult; and WHEREAS, Mr. Robinson also donated property for the Robinson Memorial and indeed stood as a testament for others, who sought the best in personal, professional, and community life, and was a source of strength and love to his family; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Mr. Robinson are his loving wife, Sara Holmes Robinson, who was originally from Selma, Alabama; sons, Joseph H. Robinson, Jr., and Richardson H. Robinson; grandsons, Ross H. Robinson, Ryan H. Robinson, Luke S. Robinson, and T. Austin Robinson; great-granddaughters, Hannah Robinson, Sara Robinson, and Skye Robinson; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA­ BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we grievously mourn the death of Joseph Robinson, Sr., and, by copy of this resolution, extend our deepest sympathy to his family, whose sor­ row we sincerely share. Senator Little (T) then requested and received unanimous consent, pursuant to the provisions of Senate Rule 35(d), in order to consider the Resolution. HOUSE MESSAGE On motion of Senator Barron, the Senate concurred in and adopted the following House amendment to the Resolution, SJR176, REGULAR SESSION 2625 30th Day - May 21, 2001 the title of which is set out in the foregoing Message from the House, to-wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR SJR176 SJR176 CREATING THE INTERIM ALABAMA METH­ AMPHETAMINE LABORATORY ERADICATION TASK FORCE. WHEREAS, there is a proliferation of illegal homemade lab­ oratories making methamphetamine, and these labs are both dan­ gerous and extremely difficult for law enforcement to locate and con- fiscate; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA­ BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That there is hereby created the Interim Alabama Methamphetamine Laboratory Eradication Task Force. The task force shall be composed of the following persons: (1) One member of the Governor’s Office appointed by the Governor. (2) One member of the Attorney General’s Office appointed by the Attorney General. (3) Three members of the Alabama Senate, one appointed by the Lieutenant Governor, one appointed by the President Pro Tem­ pore of the Senate, and one appointed by the Chair of the Senate Committee on the Judiciary. (4) Three members of the Alabama House of Representatives appointed by the Speaker of the House. The chair and vice chair of the task force shall be elected at the first meeting of the task force, which shall be called for by the Governor not later than September 1, 2001. The task force shall there­ after meet at the call of the chair or on a motion of a majority of its members. The task force shall study all aspects of how best to identify and eradicate illegal methamphetamine laboratories in the state. The task force shall present its findings, conclusions, and recommenda­ tions to the Legislature, the Governor, and the Attorney General not later than the first day of the 2002 Regular Legislative Session, at which time the task force shall stand dissolved and discharged of further duties and liabilities. 2626 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, REGULAR SESSION 2001 30th Day - May 21, 2001 No funds appropriated for the use of the Legislature may be expended for the work of the task force; however, any state, county, or municipal funds available for law enforcement projects may be used for expenses of the task force. Members shall serve without compensation, but may be reimbursed as other state employees for per diem expenses as allowed by law only to the extent that any funds are available for reimbursement of per diem expenses of the members, not to exceed a total of five thousand dollars ($5,000). Notwithstanding the foregoing, no legislative member may receive state per diem for a meeting of the task force when the Legislature is in session or if a legislative member is being paid any other payments on the same dates for attendance of other state business.

context_synopsis: A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT To require that a pharmacist dispensing medication to a patient covered by PEEHIP or an insurance policy of the State Em­ ployees Insurance Board prescribe a generic equivalent medication when available. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. As a condition of participation in the Public Edu­ cation Employees Health Insurance Programs (PEEHIP), or an in­ surance policy of the State Employees Insurance Board (SEIB) a pharmacist shall dispense a generic equivalent medication to fill a prescription for a patient covered by PEEHIP or SEIB when one is available unless the physician indicates in longhand writing on the prescription “medically Necessary” or “dispense as written” or “do not substitute”. The generic equivalent drug product dispensed shall be pharmaceutically and therapeutically equivalent and contain the same active ingredient, or ingredients and shall be of the same dos­ age, form, and strength. Section 2. This act shall become effective on the first day of the third month following its passage and approval by the Governor, or its otherwise becoming law. Which was adopted.

Senator Dial then offered the following substitute for the Bill, SB12, as amended, to-wit: 908 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, REGULAR SESSION 2002 19th Day - March 5, 2002 SUBSTITUTE FOR SB12, AS AMENDED A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT To amend Sections 16-64-4 and 16-64-5, Code of Alabama 1975, relating to nonresident student tuition rates; to provide that in­ stitutions of higher education may establish tuition rates of nonresi­ dent undergraduate students for a two-year period. BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA: Section 1. Sections 16-64-4 and 16-64-5, Code of Alabama 1975, are amended to read as follows: “§16-64-4. “(a) Each Alabama public institution of higher education shall charge each undergraduate student who is registered as a nonresident a minimum of two times the resident tuition rate charged by that in­ stitution. This rate shall be effective for students who register at an institution beginning August 1, 1997. A nonresident graduate student at an institution shall be charged a rate of tuition that is at least at the level of tuition charged to a nonresident undergraduate. “(b) The above mandatory tuition rates shall be suspended for a period of two years beginning on the effective date of this act and tuition during that time shall be as established by the institutions pursuant to Section 16-45-5 Code of Alabama 1975. “(b) (c) The governing boards of each four-year public institution of higher education shall retain the power to extend resident tuition rates to students who reside in any county within 50 miles of a campus of the institution; provided, however, that campus must be in existence and operating as of January 1, 1996. For public two-year institutions, the State Board of Education, upon the recom­ mendation of the Chancellor of the Department of Postsecondary Education, shall retain the power to extend resident tuition rates to students who reside in any county within 50 miles of a campus of the institution; provided, however, that campus must be in existence and operating as of January 1, 1996.” “§16-64-5. “A four-year public institution of higher education, at the discretion of its governing board and a two-year public institution of REGULAR SESSION 2002 909 19th Day - March 5, 2002 higher education at the discretion of the Chancellor of the Depart­ ment of Postsecondary Education may elect to adopt policies regard­ ing nonresident tuition which are more rigorous than those specified in this chapter.” Section 2. The provisions of this act shall expire two years after the effective date of this act. Section 3. This act shall become effective immediately upon its passage and approval by the Governor, or its otherwise becoming law. Which was adopted.

Section 1. The following amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, is proposed and shall become valid as a part of the Constitution when all requirements of this act are fulfilled: PROPOSED AMENDMENT No person elected or appointed sheriff, or any elected or appointed Jackson County official may assume a supernumerary office after the effective date of this amendment. Any person who, on the effective date of this amendment, is entitled to participate in a supernumerary program may continue to participate in that super­ numerary program, which shall include the assumption of a super­ numerary office according to the terms and conditions of the law which established that supernumerary program. Every elected or ap­ pointed Jackson County official may participate in the Employees’ Retirement System of Alabama upon the same terms and conditions as may be specified by law for any other employee in the same re­ tirement system. Jackson County officials holding office at the time of the ratification of this amendment shall be eligible to purchase service credit in the Employees’ Retirement System for the time the official has served in the current office. For the purposes of this amendment, the words “elected or appointed county official” shall include, subject only to express limitation, any person elected to rep­ 1506 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, REGULAR SESSION 2002 25th Day - April 2, 2002 resent Jackson County in any representation body of the state and in­ cludes any person appointed to serve the remaining term of an elected or appointed county official, but shall not include a judge, district attorney, constable, school board member, or any official elected from a judicial circuit. Section 2. An election upon the proposed amendment shall be held in accordance with Amendment 555 to the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, and the election laws of this state. Section 3. The appropriate election official shall assign a bal­ lot number for the proposed constitutional amendment on the election ballot and shall set forth the following description of the substance or subject matter of the proposed constitutional amendment: “Relating to Jackson County, proposing an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, to phase out the supernumerary system for certain elected public officials and allow them to participate in the Employees’ Retirement System. WHEREAS, the Alabama Legislature is deeply saddened at the death of Mr. Charles Molton Williams of Birmingham, Alabama, on January 6, 2004, at the age of 73 years; and WHEREAS, born June 21, 1930, in Birmingham, Mr. Will- iams received a Bachelor of Science Degree in Business Administra- tion from Washington and Lee University in 1952; he later joined the business founded by his grandfather and became President of Molton, Allen, and Williams, Inc., in 1968 and Chairman of the Board in 1978; he was the founding Chairman of Brigham-Williams and As- sociates, Inc., which later became RealtySouth; and WHEREAS, deeply involved in prison ministry, Mr. Will- iams was a member of South Highland Presbyterian Church for over 50 years and founded Re-Entry Ministries, Inc., an outreach program that assists ex-inmates; he also served as Chairman and Chief Exec- utive Officer of Cornerstone Schools of Alabama, Inc., which offers religious oriented education to inner-city children; and WHEREAS, some of the numerous civic activities of Mr. Williams include membership in the Downtown Kiwanis Club, and leadership positions with the Birmingham Festival of Arts Associa- tion; the Baptist Hospitals Advisory Board; Boys and Girls Clubs of Central Alabama, Inc.; the Salvation Army Advisory Board; Impact Family Counseling, Inc.; and Kairos; he also was a member of the Country Club of Birmingham, The Club, and the Redstone Club; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the memory of Molton Williams are his devoted wife, Hope; children, Charles M. Williams, Jr. (Kath- leen); J. T. Hunter Williams (Gini); John W. Williams (Beth); and Kate Hope Williams Simpson (Charles); grandchildren, Claire Eve- lyn Williams; Charles Molton Williams, III; Thomas Hunter Molton Williams; Donald Porter Williams; John White Williams, Jr.; Mari- anne Coston Williams; Hope White Simpson; Charles Hatcher Sim- pson, Jr.; and Samuel Day Simpson; and WHEREAS, the illustrious record of Charles Molton Will- iams’s personal, public, and civic achievements have indeed earned for him the respect of his family, friends, and the community; now therefore, 124 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 2nd Day - February 5, 2004 BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That in sad- ness and regret the death of Mr. Charles Molton Williams of Bir- mingham, Alabama, is hereby recorded and deepest sympathy is extended to his wife for whom a copy of this resolution shall be pro- vided. Senator French requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

WHEREAS, recorded with deep and abiding sorrow is the la- mentable death of Mr. Bill Roper, Minister of Music for First Baptist Church in Montgomery, Alabama, on January 24, 2004, at the age of 66 years; and WHEREAS, with his sincere dedication and love for music, Mr. Roper served his Lord and Savior Jesus Christ as Minister of Mu- sic at First Baptist Church for 32 years, and as director and creator of the annual Living Christmas Tree program for 23 years, his trium- phant and beautiful musical presentations were attended by countless individuals from near and far; and WHEREAS, as Minister of Music of the Sanctuary Choir, membership increased from 50 to 164 and, with his God-given talents and musical abilities, he created the School of Fine Arts at First Bap- tist Church in 1984, which offers lessons in numerous and varied mu- sical programs, including voice, piano, organ, and guitar; and 132 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 2nd Day - February 5, 2004 WHEREAS, Mr. Roper often used affirming references to faith and God in his conversations and offered immense pleasure to church members and visitors at First Baptist Church by selecting hymns and songs for individuals of all ages and walks of life; and WHEREAS, left to cherish the precious memory of Mr. Bill Roper are his devoted wife of 42 years, Patty Phillips Roper; daugh- ters, Beth (Benjy) Harris and Kathy (Mike) Shirley; four grandchil- dren; a sister; and other close family members and friends; now there- fore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That, in praise and gratitude, we hereby honor the life and service of Mr. Bill Roper, Minister of Music at First Baptist Church in Montgomery, Al- abama, who will live forever in the hearts and minds of all those whose lives he touched, and extend heartfelt sympathy to his wife, for whom a copy of this resolution is provided that she may know of our shared sorrow in her great and inconsolable loss. recovered_synopsis: REQUESTING U.S. GOVERNMENTAL OFFI- CIALS TO SUPPORT ACCESSIBILITY AND COMMUNICA- TION ISSUES CONCERNING DEAF AND HARD OF HEARING CITIZENS. WHEREAS, the Americans With Disabilities Act of 1990 was intended to ensure accessibility to the mainstream of life for all persons with disabilities, including all aspects of public communica- tion for people who are deaf or hard of hearing; however, 14 years af- ter enactment of the law, widespread adoption of captioning stan- dards in all audible media and the nation’s public facilities has yet to reach acceptable standards; and WHEREAS, the absence of captioning in various areas such as emergency notification systems, movie theaters, airport visuals and in-flight movies, train and transit communication, television pro- gramming, and more are still evident; and WHEREAS, at a time when there is an increasing need for ex- panded captioning services that address the accessibility issues put forth in the Americans With Disabilities Act, recent actions by the U.S. Department of Education have resulted in censorship of televi- sion programs selected for captioning, as recommended by a deaf consumer advisory board and to be financed with allocated federal funds; and WHEREAS, the Alabama Legislature proudly recognizes the contributions and accomplishments of people who are deaf in the State of Alabama and acknowledges the significant rights of all per- sons with disabilities to equal accessibility to public communication and facilities; and WHEREAS, this legislative body thinks it is proper to request 1362 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 21st Day - April 15, 2004 U.S. Government officials to take appropriate action to better ensure that the rights of deaf and hard of hearing citizens are considered and protected; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we are in full support of ideals advanced by the Alabama Association of the Deaf, which advocates for appropriate accessibility in public commu- nication, and we request the U.S. Department of Education to guard against censorship of captioned programming to the greatest extent possible. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we respectfully request that President George Bush and the Alabama U.S. Congressional Delegation provide leadership and support for expanded accessibility in public facilities and for communication issues concerning the 28 million Americans who are deaf or hard of hearing. A copy of this resolution shall be provided to the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Education, the President of the United States, and each member of the Alabama U.S. Congressional Delegation so that our concerns re- garding this important matter are known. Senator Poole requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

and WHEREAS, contact with a contaminated needle used in tat- tooing, ear or body piercing, or intravenous drug use and sexual con- tact with an infected partner are frequent sources of infection; and WHEREAS, a national study published in the October 1995 issue of the Journal of American Medical Association shows that Hepatitis B vaccine saves lives and is cost-effective by preventing costly liver disease and liver transplants; recovered_synopsis: CREATING A JOINT LEGISLATIVE COMMIT- TEE FOR THE ALABAMA CHAMBER AUTOMATION SYS- TEM WHEREAS, the Alabama Legislature is presently in need to upgrade the Alabama Chamber Automation System (ACAS) for use by the members of the Alabama Legislature beginning with the Reg- ular Session of 2005, and, 2374 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2004 30th Day - May 17, 2004 WHEREAS, there is a need for policies and procedures to be formalized prior to the upgrade of ACAS at the beginning of the Reg- ular Session of 2005; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That there is hereby created a joint interim legislative committee for the Alabama Chamber Automation System (ACAS). The committee shall be com- posed of three (3) members of the Senate appointed by the Lt. Gov- ernor and the President Pro Tempore; three (3) members of the House of Representatives appointed by the Speaker; the Clerk of the House of Representatives or his designee; and the Secretary of the Senate or his designee. The chair and vice chair of the committee shall be elect- ed at the first meeting of the committee; the committee shall formal- ize policies and procedures for the use of laptop computers by the membership of the Alabama Legislature. The committee shall advise the Clerk of the House and the Secretary of the Senate with regard to the information enhancements needed on the ACAS system. The leg- islative members of the ACAS Joint Interim Legislative Committee shall serve as the pilot project testees when the upgrade is ready for testing prior to the 2005 Regular Session. Upon the request of the chair, the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House shall provide the clerical assistance necessary for the committee’s work. Each member of the committee shall be en- titled to his or her regular legislative compensation, his or her per di- em, and travel expenses for each day he or she attends a meeting of the committee which shall be paid out of any funds appropriated to the use of the Legislature, upon warrants drawn on the State Comp- troller upon requisitions signed by the chair of the committee. Not- withstanding the foregoing, no member shall receive additional leg- islative compensation or per diem when the Legislature is in session or if a member is being paid any other payments on the same dates for attendance of other state business. The committee shall stand dis- solved and discharged of any further duties and liabilities at the end of the Regular Session of 2006. The total expenditure of the commit- tee shall not exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000.00). recovered_synopsis: RECOGNIZING THE 50TH ANNIVERSARY OF BROWN V. BOARD OF EDUCATION AND ENCOURAGING FURTHER COMMITMENT TO ITS PRINCIPLES AND PURPOS- ES. REGULAR SESSION 2399 30th Day - May 17, 2004 WHEREAS, today, May 17, 2004, marks the 50th Anniversa- ry of the landmark U.S. Supreme Court case of Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, Kansas, which held unconstitutional the previ- ously existing “separate but equal” doctrine of racially segregated schools in this country; and WHEREAS, many credit this decision as sparking the civil rights movement and leading to the enactment of federal and state laws that ended official discrimination and segregation; indeed, the legacy of this opinion was the reaffirmation of the principles of the 14th Amendment to the Constitution of the United States regarding the rights of all Americans to equal protection of the law; and WHEREAS, significant progress has been made in the years since 1954, and today, more than ever, Alabamians judge each other not by the color of their skins but by the content of their character; yet, as in most endeavors, there is room for additional improvement and advancement concerning this most fundamental freedom; and WHEREAS, it is fortunate that, on this most significant anni- versary date, we may acknowledge the importance of this case and its impact on our nation and state, and that we may encourage govern- mental and educational leaders to further dedicate and devote their energies and resources to achieving the preeminent precepts therein contained; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we, in concert and conjunction with the Legislative Black Caucus, recog- nize the historic and cultural significance of the 50th Anniversary of the landmark decision of Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, Kansas. President George Bush, Governor Bob Riley, governmental officials, and state educational officials are respectfully requested to strive on a daily basis to completely fulfill the just and right principle of equality for all as advocated and advanced by this judicial decision in order that no child or adult will be left behind. A copy of this res- olution shall be provided to President Bush, Governor Riley, the State Board of Education, state and local superintendents of education, and members of state boards of trustees, so that these officials may know of and share these sentiments with other governmental and educa- tional officials. recovered_synopsis: RECOGNIZING THE MONTH OF MARCH AS THE SELMA TO MONTGOMERY MARCH/NATIONAL VOT- ING RIGHTS CELEBRATION MONTH AND THE WEEKEND OF MARCH 4-6, 2005, ON THE 40TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE VOTING RIGHTS MARCH IN ALABAMA. WHEREAS, on Sunday, March 7, 1965, citizens participating in a peaceful march while seeking their voting rights were beaten as they attempted to cross the Edmond Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama; and WHEREAS, on March 21, 1965, the Selma to Montgomery March brought international attention to the cause of voter regis- tration in the State of Alabama; and WHEREAS, over 25,000 people marched together in a fight for the right to vote, freely and fairly from any harassment or dis- crimination; and WHEREAS, due in part to the efforts of the participants in the Selma to Montgomery March, Congress promptly enacted the Voting Rights Act of 1965, thereby ensuring the right of all citizens to vote; and WHEREAS, the Selma to Montgomery March inspired people from nations all over the world, including South Africa and Poland, to proclaim and fight for their right to vote and is an international symbol for the right to vote; and WHEREAS, the Selma to Montgomery March solidified America as a true democracy by providing the impetus by which all citizens of the United States of America are allowed to exercise their basic constitutional right to vote; and 418 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2005 10th Day - March 3, 2005 WHEREAS, the rich history and fame surrounding the Selma to Montgomery March have had a tremendous impact on educating people about voting rights and have resulted in the promotion of tourism and economic development in the State of Alabama; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby recognize the month of March, in 2005, and in each succeeding year, as the Selma to Montgomery March/National Voting Rights Celebration Month in Alabama and that we further recognize the weekend of March 4-6 in 2005, on the 40th Anniversary of the historic voting rights march in Alabama. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we urge the citizens of Alabama to reflect on the history surrounding the march and the tremendous impact it had making America a true democracy and creating a more fair and just society for all. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we urge the U.S. Congress to renew the Voting Rights Act of 1965. The Standing Committee on Rules reported the following amendment to the Resolution, HJR126, to wit: AMENDMENT TO HJR126 On page 1, after line 25, insert the following language: “BE IT RESOLVED FURTHER, That we hereby request that Governor Bob Riley immediately grant to Governor Guy Hunt the Governor’s Councillor status pursuant to Section 36-13-13, Code of Alabama 1975, and that a copy of this resolution be forwarded to Governor Riley that he may know of our desires in this matter.” Which was adopted.

recovered_synopsis: CREATING THE SPECIAL TASK FORCE ON CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE. WHEREAS, it is generally recognized that a significant num- ber of the population of the State of Alabama has a form of chronic kidney disease, including persons with seriously reduced kidney function that may progress to End Stage Renal Disease, ESRD, requiring kidney dialysis or the receipt of a kidney by transplant; and WHEREAS, ESRD is usually the result of years of chronic kidney disease caused by diabetes, high blood pressure, or a family history of chronic kidney disease as the primary contributing factors; and WHEREAS, we recognize that the treatment of chronic kid- ney disease is a tremendous expense and that the early diagnosis and effective treatment of chronic kidney disease can prolong lives and delay the high cost of treatment, including dialysis or transplantation, or both, and that there are existing, cost-effective laboratory test cal- culations that can assist in the early diagnosis of chronic kidney dis- ease; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the Special Task Force on Chronic Kidney Disease is created. The task force shall be composed of six physicians licensed to practice medi- cine appointed by the Medical Association of the State of Alabama, two of whom shall be primary care physicians, two of whom shall be nephrologists, and two of whom shall be pathologists. The presiding officer of the House of Representatives shall appoint two members who represent the state affiliate of the National Kidney Foundation, one of whom shall be an advocate or patient on dialysis or a transplant recipient and shall appoint one member who represents the Depart- ment of Nephrology at the University of Alabama Medical Center or his or her designee. The presiding officer of the Senate shall appoint one member who represents owners or operators of clinical laborato- ries in the state and one member who represents the Alabama Hospi- tal Association. The Governor shall appoint one member represent- ing a health care services plan provider and one member from a list of five names submitted by the Business Council of Alabama. The State Health Officer or his or her designee shall serve as chair of the task force. The task force shall study all facets of chronic kidney dis- ease and its complications and how it affects the citizens of Alabama. In conducting such study, the task force shall study best practices 2192 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 28th Day - April 6, 2006 based on Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative K/DOQI Clin- ical Practice Guidelines or other medically recognized clinical prac- tice guidelines for chronic kidney disease. Additionally, the task force shall make recommendations on the implementation of a cost- effective plan for early screening, diagnosis, and treatment for the cit- izens of Alabama that are at risk for chronic kidney disease. The task force shall meet for the purpose of organizing within 45 days of the effective date of this resolution and may enter into agreements with state agencies and public or private organizations for such additional staff or support as the task force may determine to be necessary. Any and all private funding shall be accepted only upon a clear designa- tion that such funding place no conditions on the findings or recom- mendations of the task force. RESOLVED FURTHER, The task force shall recommend to the Legislature not later than the first legislative day of the 2007 Reg- ular Session. Nothing contained in the recommendations shall be construed as a mandate to provide any new or additional coverage by any health care insurer or health care service plan. However, the pre- ceding provision does not negate suggestions or recommendations that have been voted on and passed by members of the task force. The task force shall stand dissolved and discharged of any further duties and liabilities on July 1, 2007, unless it is affirmatively renewed before such time. Each member of the task force who is a state employee or state official shall be entitled to receive a per diem and travel allowance in the same amount as is received by other state employees traveling on official state business. The total expenditures of the task force for its business shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000).

WHEREAS, it is generally recognized that a significant num- ber of the population of the State of Alabama has a form of chronic kidney disease, including persons with seriously reduced kidney function that may progress to End Stage Renal Disease, ESRD, requiring kidney dialysis or the receipt of a kidney by transplant; and WHEREAS, ESRD is usually the result of years of chronic kidney disease caused by diabetes, high blood pressure, or a family history of chronic kidney disease as the primary contributing factors; and WHEREAS, we recognize that the treatment of chronic kid- ney disease is a tremendous expense and that the early diagnosis and effective treatment of chronic kidney disease can prolong lives and delay the high cost of treatment, including dialysis or transplantation, or both, and that there are existing, cost-effective laboratory test cal- culations that can assist in the early diagnosis of chronic kidney dis- ease; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the Special Task Force on Chronic Kidney Disease is created. The task force shall be composed of six physicians licensed to practice medi- cine appointed by the Medical Association of the State of Alabama, two of whom shall be primary care physicians, two of whom shall be nephrologists, and two of whom shall be pathologists. The presiding officer of the House of Representatives shall appoint two members who represent the state affiliate of the National Kidney Foundation, one of whom shall be an advocate or patient on dialysis or a transplant recipient and shall appoint one member who represents the Depart- ment of Nephrology at the University of Alabama Medical Center or his or her designee. The presiding officer of the Senate shall appoint one member who represents owners or operators of clinical laborato- ries in the state and one member who represents the Alabama Hospi- tal Association. The Governor shall appoint one member represent- ing a health care services plan provider and one member from a list of five names submitted by the Business Council of Alabama. The State Health Officer or his or her designee shall serve as chair of the task force. The task force shall study all facets of chronic kidney dis- ease and its complications and how it affects the citizens of Alabama. In conducting such study, the task force shall study best practices 2192 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 28th Day - April 6, 2006 based on Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative K/DOQI Clin- ical Practice Guidelines or other medically recognized clinical prac- tice guidelines for chronic kidney disease. Additionally, the task force shall make recommendations on the implementation of a cost- effective plan for early screening, diagnosis, and treatment for the cit- izens of Alabama that are at risk for chronic kidney disease. The task force shall meet for the purpose of organizing within 45 days of the effective date of this resolution and may enter into agreements with state agencies and public or private organizations for such additional staff or support as the task force may determine to be necessary. Any and all private funding shall be accepted only upon a clear designa- tion that such funding place no conditions on the findings or recom- mendations of the task force. RESOLVED FURTHER, The task force shall recommend to the Legislature not later than the first legislative day of the 2007 Reg- ular Session. Nothing contained in the recommendations shall be construed as a mandate to provide any new or additional coverage by any health care insurer or health care service plan. However, the pre- ceding provision does not negate suggestions or recommendations that have been voted on and passed by members of the task force. The task force shall stand dissolved and discharged of any further duties and liabilities on July 1, 2007, unless it is affirmatively renewed before such time. Each member of the task force who is a state employee or state official shall be entitled to receive a per diem and travel allowance in the same amount as is received by other state employees traveling on official state business. The total expenditures of the task force for its business shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000).

recovered_synopsis: SUPPORTING GOVERNOR RILEY’S CALL FOR A BOYCOTT OF TRAVEL TO ARUBA. WHEREAS, on May 30, 2005, Natalee Holloway, an 18- year-old Alabama citizen, disappeared on the island of Aruba; and WHEREAS, for many months now the citizens of Alabama have been both saddened by Natalee’s disappearance and inspired by her family and their resolve to find the truth and find their daughter; and WHEREAS, as the months passed, it became increasingly clear that Aruba’s investigation of Natalee’s disappearance has been plagued with an unacceptable amount of missteps, miscommunica- tions, and inconsistencies, as numerous suspects have been detained, but then released, without the benefit of gaining any new information that has helped find our missing fellow American; and WHEREAS, Governor Riley has recognized with apprecia- REGULAR SESSION 233 4th Day - January 19, 2006 tion the efforts of many private citizens of Aruba for their assistance in the search for Natalee; however, on November 17, 2005, after care- ful consideration of the official actions of the government of Aruba, Governor Riley, joined by Natalee’s family, urged all Americans to avoid travel to Aruba; and WHEREAS, subsequently, on November 22, 2005, Governor Riley also asked other Governors to urge their citizens to avoid travel to Aruba in hopes that a boycott would cause the Aruban people to demand that their public officials conduct the investigation of Nata- lee’s disappearance in a more careful, thorough, and appropriate manner; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the Legislature heartily supports Governor Riley in this difficult but well-founded decision to urge a boycott of travel to Aruba. BE IT RESOLVED FURTHER, That the Legislature provide a copy of this resolution to Governor Riley as a show of its support of his actions. On motion of Senator French, the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

recovered_synopsis: STRONGLY URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS TO OBEY AND ENFORCE STATE COAL MINING LAWS. GREG PAPPAS, Clerk. On motion of Senator Smitherman, the Senate concurred in and adopted the following House amendment to the Resolution, SJR19, the title of which is set out in the foregoing Message from the House, to wit: SUBSTITUTE FOR SJR19 SJR19 STRONGLY URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS TO OBEY AND ENFORCE STATE COAL MINING LAWS. WHEREAS, from 2001 to present, there have been 21 fatali- ties in the Alabama mining industry; and WHEREAS, currently there are 2.4 mine inspectors in the Department of Industrial Relations Mine Safety Program, down from 6.5 in 2001, and only 791 of the lawfully required 1,705 inspections were completed in 2004; and WHEREAS, there are 509 mines in Alabama of which 9 are operating underground coal mines, the 509:3 ratio of total mines to mine inspectors in Alabama is deplorable when compared to other states: Kentucky has 519:33, Ohio has 95:29, Pennsylvania has 454:70, and West Virginia has 352:32; and WHEREAS, Chapter 9 of Title 25 of the Code of Alabama 1975, the “Alabama Coal Mine Safety Law of 1975,” is a comprehen- sive body of statutes with the stated purpose of providing “reasonable laws to promote the safety and health of those engaged in the mining of coal and for the protection and preservation of property”; and WHEREAS, specifically, Section 25-9-7 of the code provides 494 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 9th Day - Februay 7, 2006 that the “duties of mine inspectors are to make examinations of mines” and Section 25-9-20 mandates that coal mines be completely inspected at least every 45 days and “more often if necessary”; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That in the interest of public safety and the health, safety, and protection of the coal miners working in the state, the Alabama Department of Indus- trial Relations is strongly and seriously urged to obey and enforce state coal mining laws. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be immediately provided to the Director of the Alabama Depart- ment of Industrial Relations and the Director of the Division of Min- ing and Reclamation of the Alabama Department of Industrial Relations as an indication of our profound sentiment on this issue.

recovered_synopsis: URGING MUNICIPALITIES IN JEFFERSON COUNTY NOT TO INCREASE FEES PAID TO STORM WASTE MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY AND REJECT ANY PRIOR DE- CISION MADE TO INCREASE SUCH FEES. WHEREAS, several municipalities in Jefferson County have been requested to increase fees paid to the Storm Waste Management Authority (SWMA) pursuant to a new draft permit under consider- ation by the Alabama Department of Environmental Management (ADEM); and 218 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 4th Day - January 19, 2006 WHEREAS, local municipal governments are authorized, but not required, to participate in the program of the authority pursuant to Title 11, Chapter 89C, Code of Alabama 1975, as one alternative for the management of stormwater in compliance with the EPA National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES); and WHEREAS, another alternative for NPDES compliance is a cooperative government program in which ADEM would work with local governments in meeting their compliance issues; and WHEREAS, ADEM has a long history of working with EPA- regulated local entities to ensure that the entities are fully informed on compliance requirements; and WHEREAS, merely participating in the SWMA program does not relieve any municipality of its stormwater liability issues re- lated to NPDES compliance; and WHEREAS, a local governmental entity can obtain an indi- vidual NPDES water permit without SWMA participation; and WHEREAS, considering the alternatives to NPDES compli- ance, the SWMA should be considered an additional, not exclusive, method of achieving compliance; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That the mu- nicipalities in Jefferson County participating in the Storm Waste Management Authority (SWMA) for NPDES compliance are hereby urged to resist increased SWMA participation fees, and to reject or void any prior decision to pay increased SWMA participation fees until all options, including a voluntary cooperative government pro- gram, are considered for NPDES issues. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be provided to ADEM and to the governing body of each affect- ed municipality. Nothing we have said here indicates that such study of the Bible or of religion, when presented objectively as a part of a secular program of education, may not be effected consis- tently with the First Amendment”; and WHEREAS, the United States Supreme Court has also stated that it is not unconstitutional for the Bible to be used in the appropri- ate study of subjects such as literature, history, civilization, ethics, and similar disciplines; and WHEREAS, the State of Alabama Department of Educa- tions’s Subject and Personnel Code currently lists a course in the Bi- ble as Literature as an approved elective; and WHEREAS, the study of the Bible can offer a fundamental understanding of the influence of the Bible on literature, history, law, and American community life and culture; and WHEREAS, the study of the Bible can provide a greater knowledge of Middle Eastern history, geography, religion, and poli- tics; and WHEREAS, without imposing the doctrines of any particular religious sect, such studies can be used to inform the students of Al- abama of the importance of religion in world and national history; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we strongly encourage the study of the Bible as an elective in city, coun- ty, or other local schools and in private schools in a manner not in- consistent with the Constitution of the United States of America and the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, in order to promote academic excellence and cultural literacy. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That if a local board of edu- cation wishes to develop and implement the study of the Bible as an elective course, the course should meet all State Board of Education standards for district-approved electives. REGULAR SESSION 411 7th Day - January 31, 2006 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be transmitted to the State Superintendent of Education, so that its contents may be known to the superintendent of each local public school system. Senator Erwin requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.
