WHEREAS, from 4:30 p.m. on February 2, 2006, to 5:00 a.m. on February 3, 2006, five churches in Bibb County were intentionally burned in what fire investigators are calling the worst incidence of church arson since the outbreak of over 100 church fires in the 1990s; and WHEREAS, in addition to the despicable acts of one or more hateful and cowardly arsonists, a sixth church, New Harmony Baptist Church in Chilton County, also tragically sustained fire damage, but it was determined that the Chilton County church fire was not an act of arson; and 522 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 9th Day - Februay 7, 2006 WHEREAS, the spate of fires damaged or destroyed Reho- beth Baptist Church, Ashby Baptist Church, Old Union Baptist Church, Pleasant Sabine Baptist Church, and Antioch Baptist Church in Bibb County, and New Harmony Baptist Church in Chilton Coun- ty, disrupting the lives of about 550 members of the congregations of all churches combined; and WHEREAS, it has been reported that on Tuesday, February 7, 2006, that fire erupted at four more rural Alabama churches, and arson is suspected concerning Dancy Baptist Church, south of Aliceville in Pickens County, Spring Valley Baptist Church, near Emelle in Sumter County, Morning Star Baptist Church near Boligee in Greene County, and Galilee Baptist Church near Panola in Sumter County; and WHEREAS, a motive or motives have yet to be attributed to these senseless acts of destruction and violence; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That we hereby condemn these deplorable acts of arson and support federal and state law enforcement and the judicial system in the swift capture and punishment of the perpetrator or perpetrators of these heinous acts. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That we express our deepest heartfelt sympathy and condolences for the church members of all of the churches affected by this tragic string of events. Senator Singleton requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

recovered_synopsis: APPLYING TO THE UNITED STATES CON- GRESS FOR A CONVENTION TO PROPOSE AN AMENDMENT TO THE CONSTITUTION OF THE UNITED STATES. BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That this Legislature, pursuant to Article V of the Constitution of the United States, hereby makes application to the Congress of the United States to call a convention for the purpose of adopting the following amendment to the Constitution of the United States: Proposed Amendment: Section 1. This amendment may be cited as the “Marriage 770 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE, 2006 14th Day - February 22, 2006 Protection Amendment.” Section 2. Marriage in the United States shall consist only of the union of a man and a woman. Neither this Constitution, nor the constitution of any State, shall be construed to require that marriage or the legal incidents thereof be conferred upon any union other than of a man and a woman. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That this application by the Legislature of the State of Alabama constitutes a continuing application in accordance with Article V of the Constitution of the United States until at least two-thirds of the legislatures of the several states have made similar applications pursuant to Article V. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That since this method of proposing amendments to the Constitution has never been completed to the point of calling a convention and no interpretation of the power of the states in the exercise of this right has ever been made by any court or any qualified tribunal, and since the exercise of the power is a matter of basic sovereign right and the interpretation thereof is primarily in the sovereign government making the exercise, and since the power to use the right in full also carries the power to use the right in part, the Legislature of the State of Alabama interprets Article V to mean that if two-thirds of the states make application for a convention to propose an identical amendment to the Constitution for ratification with a limitation that such an amendment would be the only matter before it; that such a convention would have power only to propose the specified amendment and would be limited to such a proposal; and would not have power to vary the text thereof or propose other amendments on the same or a different proposition. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a duly attested copy of this resolution be immediately transmitted to the Secretary of the Senate of the United States, the Clerk of the House of Representatives of the United States, to each member of the Alabama Congressional Delegation, and to each house of each State Legislature in the United States. Senator Mitchell requested and received unanimous consent to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

recovered_synopsis: RECOGNIZING THE BRUNDIDGE HISTORI- CAL SOCIETY’S “COME HOME, IT’S SUPPERTIME” AS ALA- BAMA’S ORIGINAL AND OFFICIAL FOLKLIFE PLAY. WHEREAS, the Brundidge Historical Society’s “Come Home, It’s Suppertime” is hereby recognized as Alabama’s Original and Official Folklife Play; and WHEREAS, in the spring of 2002, the Brundidge Historical Society presented the premier production of its “Come Home, It’s Suppertime”; the play was the realization of an eight-year dream of not only bringing community theater to Brundidge, but preserving the historic city hall building where the play is presented as the corner- stone of the town; and WHEREAS, the historic city hall building was constructed in 1940 as a Works Progress Administration project, and dubbed We Piddle Around because some believed that the WPA workers piddled around instead of working; it was gutted by fire in the early 1990s and has been magically turned into a unique community theater now known as the “We Piddle Around Theater”; and WHEREAS, centered around the Great Depression era, the play, from the original script, tells the story of the hardships, strug- gles, and perseverance of the people who lived during “Hoover Days” in a delightful, entertaining way; the stories are told by those who lived them and the original music is coupled with period songs and traditional hymns; there have been over 68 sold-out performanc- es; groups come from as far as Birmingham and Atlanta to see an unforgettable performance and dine on fried chicken, sweet ’taters, peas, turnips, cornbread, and blackberry pie; and WHEREAS, “Come Home, It’s Suppertime” is a unique sup- per theater experience and has brought great recognition to this small South Alabama town and brings all ages, races, and religions together to tell the story of a community; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That Senator Wendell Mitchell and Representative Alan Boothe join the Alabama Legislature in recognizing the Brundidge Historical Society’s Folk- life Play, “Come Home, It’s Suppertime,” as Alabama’s Original and REGULAR SESSION 1473 23rd Day - March 28, 2006 Official Folklife Play and do request the appropriate officials to place and maintain signs or markers recognizing this play. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That a copy of this resolu- tion be provided for appropriate presentation so that this meritorious designation is known. context_synopsis: EXPRESSING THE INTENT OF THE LEGISLA- TURE REGARDING SUPERNUMERARY JUDICIAL OFFICE. WHEREAS, the Alabama Unified Court System, and the position of supernumerary, was created in 1973, by ratification of Amendment 328, the Judicial Article, of the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, now appearing as Section 155 of Article VI of the Official Recompilation of the Constitution of Alabama of 1901, as amended; and WHEREAS, the position of supernumerary was established to provide life long retirement benefits for those officers of the court to avoid interruption in court services; now therefore; BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That, in cre- ating supernumerary judicial offices, it is the intent of this body that: (1) A person is eligible for supernumerary status if he or she accumulates the required number of years of service and has contrib- uted the appropriate amount of funds into the supernumerary fund, as required by law. (2) A person who has attained supernumerary status shall for- feit that status and be barred from obtaining supernumerary status if he or she endeavors to serve in an office of profit that is different from that for which supernumerary status was originally granted. (3) A person who forfeits his or her supernumerary status pur- suant to paragraph (2) shall lose all prior service credit, may not be reinstated to his or her former supernumerary status, and shall be required to serve and contribute the appropriate number of years and amount of funds as provided in paragraph (1) to again be eligible for supernumerary status. On motion of Senator Preuitt, the Resolution, SJR146, was adopted by the Senate.

Senator Little (Z) requested and received unanimous consent in order to suspend the provisions of Senate Rule 55 and the Resolution was adopted by the Senate.

recovered_synopsis: COMMENDING FAYE COTTON FOR PROFES- SIONAL ACHIEVEMENT. WHEREAS, we take great pride and special pleasure in ex- tending highest commendation to Faye Cotton of Brilliant, Alabama, for her outstanding record of achievement during 28 years as Town Clerk; and WHEREAS, to the dismay of her colleagues and the citizens she has served so well, Mrs. Cotton has retired as Brilliant Town Clerk; she begins a new phase of her life with plans to focus on fam- ily, church, and volunteer work; and WHEREAS, when Mrs. Cotton was honored at a retirement reception, her many admirers expressed their profound regret at the loss of her beaming smile and positive attitude; the affectionate and enthusiastic praise could be overheard everywhere: well-liked, plea- sure to work with, good friend, invaluable asset, hardworking, dedi- cated, patient, sweet, wonderful, easygoing, trustworthy, helpful, dependable, not just good but the best; and WHEREAS, a native of Brilliant, born Faye Berryhill, she married Donnie Cotton and they had two children, Donna Nicholson, who is married to Tony Nicholson, and Brian Cotton, who is married to Lisa Cotton; there are six beloved grandchildren, Paige Arnold, Ja- cob Cotton, Drew Nicholson, Whitney Cotton, Brittany Dickinson, and Brandon Aaron; and three cherished great-grandchildren, Abbig- ail Dickinson, Hagen Dickinson, and Jayden Aaron; and WHEREAS, through the years Mrs. Cotton has earned wide- spread respect for her competence and commitment, as well as her many contributions to her fellow citizens in her beloved hometown; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That Faye Cotton is commended for her exemplary 28-year career as Bril- liant Town Clerk, and this resolution is offered in highest tribute to her along with best wishes for her well-deserved retirement. WHEREAS, with utmost admiration and appreciation, we recognize the LeFlore High School Girls Basketball Team, who, at the Birmingham-Jefferson Convention Complex, defeated Brewer High School 68 to 60 to claim the 2009 state title; and WHEREAS, with the championship plaque in hand, the Rat- tlers could claim vindication for their past two seasons, which ended prematurely in the South Regional in Troy; this was the school’s sec- ond title since 1994 and helped end a 15-year drought for Mobile girl teams; and WHEREAS, in the title game, the team dominated the lane, with the post players combining for an impressive 48 points, 22 re- bounds, and six rejections; the outside players flawlessly handled the ball and got it inside where the major damage was done; all associat- ed with the team played a major role in the school’s impressive 25 and 2 season and may justifiably claim a part of this coveted cham- pionship; and WHEREAS, this exceptional team is ably lead by Head Coach Darrell Walton, and his assistants Alfred Perkins, Sr., and Derrick Gray; their measured leadership instilled in these young women equal parts confidence, commitment, composure, and class; indeed these talented players bring pride to their school, Principal Thomas Reed, and the entire community; and REGULAR SESSION 1419 15th Day - March 31, 2009 WHEREAS, the 2009 Class 5A Champions are: Jacquese Brooks, Marshae Shelton, Tiffany Shelton, Brandi Mance, Gabrielle Williams, Kyra Sneed, Bessie Carson, April Webb, Jocelyn Shaw, Sarah Vann, Shanece McKinney, and Ashley Myles; now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALA- BAMA, BOTH HOUSES THEREOF CONCURRING, That with immense pleasure and great pride we commend the LeFlore High School Girls Basketball Team, the 2009 Class 5A State Champions. A copy of this resolution shall be provided to the team along with our congratulations for a job well-done.
